title: тоже, также — and и, а, но

items: {{n-g|expresses disbelief, sarcasm, irony, often combined with }}
Я]] [[там]] [[быть|был]], [[Ива́н]] '''то́же'''.|I was there and so was Ivan.

blocks.text: 1. И (and) indicates: a) Addition: *Он пилот и механик. Он читает и курит.* b) Similarity: *Он капитан, и я капитан. Здесь хорошо, и там хорошо.* 2. А (and, but) indicates: a) Difference, contrast: *Он пишет, а я читаю. Здесь хорошо, а там плохо.* b) Denial: *Он капитан, а не лейтенант. Он не пишет, а читает.* 3. Но (but) is used when the second statement somewhat limits the significance of the first one or when it introduces a statement contrary to it.
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 19.

The exercises are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. The word in brackets is the dictionary form of the missing word.
